nodes.label: Viewer
nodes.description: The human viewing the explorer SPA in a browser. They open the page, navigate flows, and curate the context bundle. Here they are the one whose page load triggers the model fetch; every tab they switch to is a view derived client-side from that single payload.

nodes.label: LoadModel
nodes.description: The SPA's boot read: fetch the whole canonical model once so every tab can be derived from it client-side. A read command (no aggregate write) issued implicitly when the explorer page mounts.

tactical.explanation: On mount, App's useEffect calls fetchModel() exactly once (empty dependency array, guarded by an `alive` flag). fetchModel does GET /api/model (api.js) and expects { model, meta }. The server route is deliberately minimal: it returns the already-resolved model plus provenance meta (source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings) straight from the closure captured at startup -- no per-request merge, no per-view endpoints. There is exactly ONE payload endpoint; the Gallery / Data-model / Glossary / Flows-board / Overview tabs are NOT separate fetches, they are re-derived from this one response. On success the payload is handed to ExplorerProvider, which memoizes the id indexes; on failure the boot card shows the error.

anchors.note: boot useEffect: fetchModel() once, [] deps, alive guard
GET /api/model -> { model, meta }
GET /api/model returns resolved.model + meta, no computation

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Built by the merge, then read by the es-view server and the view generator. Its invariants are the merge-time validations.

tactical.explanation: Served here as the in-memory snapshot resolved at server startup. resolveModel (bin/es-view.mjs main) runs once, and buildServices builds the id indexes (buildIndexes) once; the server closure holds `resolved.model` for the life of the process. GET /api/model hands the whole object back verbatim. State lives in a file (CLI: writeFileSync) or purely in memory (server path); this read flow never writes it.

anchors.note: the assembled model object
indexes built once from resolved.model at startup
resolveModel runs once; model captured for the process lifetime

nodes.label: Raw model payload
nodes.description: The whole resolved model plus provenance meta, returned as one JSON payload from GET /api/model (the same projection the MCP list_model tool exposes). The SPA holds it in a single React context and re-derives every tab from it -- it is the substrate, not a rendered view.

tactical.explanation: Shape: { model, meta:{ source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings } }. Held in ExplorerProvider, which memoizes buildIndexes(model) (nodeById/hotspotById) and galleryTypes(model) once, then exposes model+indexes to all components via context. No re-fetch happens after boot -- there is no polling, websocket, or live-reload. Every other read model in this flow is computed from THIS object in the browser via the shared selectors, with zero further server round-trips.

anchors.note: /api/model builds the { model, meta } payload
holds the payload; memoizes indexes + gallery types once

nodes.label: Flows board
nodes.description: The default tab: the left sidebar (flows grouped by tier / pivoted by actor or aggregate) plus the pan/zoom board rendering the currently selected flow's sticky lane. What the viewer reads to navigate the recovered flows.

tactical.explanation: Derived entirely client-side from the payload. Sidebar calls sidebarGroups(model, groupMode, nodeById), which pivots flows via flowNodeIds/nodeFlows into tier buckets or per-actor/per-aggregate groups. The board renders currentFlow (model.flows.find by id) and its edges. All of this reads the one in-memory model; switching flows changes React state only, never re-fetches.

anchors.note: sidebarGroups(model, groupMode, nodeById) pivots the flow list
tier / actor / aggregate grouping over model.flows
renders currentFlow + its hotspots/instances on the board

nodes.label: Data-model tab
nodes.description: The physical-layer view: the server > database > table > column containment forest with each table card showing its columns and the behavioral stickies that write / read / project it. What the viewer reads to see where data comes from.

tactical.explanation: Derived client-side: DataModel calls dataModelTree(model, nodeById) to build the containment forest (re-homing orphans under an '(unattached)' bucket) and tableConsumers(model, nodeById, tableId) to list behavioral consumers per table. Both are the SHARED selectors in src/lib/selectors.mjs, re-exported through src/web/model.js -- the identical code the server-side context/markdown renderers use, so browser and MCP projections agree.

anchors.note: imports dataModelTree + tableConsumers from model.js
shared: build the server>db>table>column forest
shared: behavioral nodes touching a table

nodes.label: Glossary tab
nodes.description: The ubiquitous language as an alphabetical dictionary: every sticky filtered by type chips and text, optionally restricted to shared (multi-flow) concepts, with letter-header navigation. What the viewer reads to learn the domain vocabulary.

tactical.explanation: Derived client-side from model.nodes: Glossary filters by active type set + query, and when sharedOnly is on keeps only nodes with nodeFlows(model,id).length > 1 (appear in more than one flow), then sorts and interleaves A-Z letter headers. Ported from buildGlossary/renderGlossaryList in generate-views.js so the SPA and the static explorer.html agree. Type chips come from galleryTypes(model).

anchors.note: filter/sort model.nodes; sharedOnly via nodeFlows
shared: flows a node appears in (drives sharedOnly)

nodes.label: Gallery tab
nodes.description: Every sticky in the model as a filterable grid: type chips plus text search, sorted by palette type order then label. What the viewer reads to browse the full node set regardless of flow.

tactical.explanation: Derived client-side: Gallery filters model.nodes by the active type set + query and sorts by galleryTypes(model) index then label. galleryTypes(model) (src/web/model.js) lists the types actually present in palette order and drives both the filter chips and the sort. Ported from buildGallery/renderGrid in generate-views.js. No server call -- pure re-derivation of the one payload.

anchors.note: filter/sort model.nodes by type chips + query
types present in palette order; drives chips + sort

flows.name: Viewer opens the explorer and the SPA loads the whole model once
flows.summary: The viewer opens the es-view explorer in a browser. On mount the SPA fetches GET /api/model exactly once and the server returns the entire resolved model plus provenance meta from the snapshot it captured at startup -- minimal server work, one endpoint, no per-view queries. The SPA holds that single payload in one React context and re-derives every tab client-side (Flows board, Gallery, Data model, Glossary, Overview) via selectors shared with the server. The point is that the server is a thin model transport and the explorer's richness is all client-side derivation over ONE response.
flows.trigger: The viewer opens the es-view URL in a browser; the React App mounts and its boot useEffect fires.

hotspots.label: The explorer loads the model once at boot; edits need a page reload AND a server restart
hotspots.description: The SPA fetches /api/model exactly once (App boot useEffect, empty deps) and never re-fetches -- no polling, websocket, or live-reload. The server serves the model snapshot resolved at startup and builds its indexes eagerly, so it never picks up file changes either. Result: after editing flows.json (or the traces feeding --traces), the viewer sees nothing new until the operator BOTH restarts es-view (to re-resolve + re-index) AND reloads the page (to re-fetch). Human question: is a one-shot frozen boot acceptable for the curate-while-you-work loop this tool is built for, or should es-view watch the model file and the SPA poll / offer a reload affordance?

tactical.explanation: App.jsx useEffect has [] deps and an alive guard -- exactly one fetch per page load, no interval or socket. server.mjs GET /api/model returns resolved.model captured in the createServer closure; buildServices runs buildIndexes once at startup (bin/es-view.mjs main); resolveModel likewise runs once. Nothing invalidates or rebuilds either the payload or the indexes for the process lifetime.

anchors.note: single boot fetch, [] deps, no re-fetch path
returns the startup model snapshot verbatim
indexes built once, never invalidated
